ui high [panel]: The part-number rows split the text in the wrong place. The regex in pnRow takes the first word as the number, so 'Motorcraft GL-456', 'Lester 8260' and 'Gates 42294' show the brand name in large monospace and the real number in small grey text. data-pn is set to that first word, so tapping 'copy' copies 'Motorcraft' or 'Lester' instead of the number. You can see this in ui-panel-phone, ui-panel-desk and ui-panel-flagged-desk. -> In pnRow, check whether the first word contains no digits (/^[A-Za-z]+$/). If so, treat it as the brand: render <small class=brand>Motorcraft</small> first and the number (the first word that contains a digit, e.g. GL-456) as the <span>. Set data-pn to that number. Brand rows then show as 'GL-456 · Motorcraft', and copy grabs GL-456.

ui high [visual]: On the phone, the Explode dial sits on top of every open sheet (z-index 7, background #141414ee, which is almost opaque). It covers the last visible part number, list row or paragraph, and text shows faintly through it (ui-panel-phone, ui-list-phone, ui-systems-phone, ui-help-phone). The dial does nothing useful while you are reading a sheet. -> In open(), add document.body.classList.add('sheet-open'); in closeAll(), remove it. Add CSS: @media(max-width:700px){body.sheet-open #dial,body.sheet-open #hint{display:none} .sheet{padding-bottom:calc(20px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))}}

ui high [first-run]: The Help sheet explains controls that don't exist. It lists 'Filter', 'Body', 'X-ray' and '+ Part / Data', but the real UI has 'View: Full' (which cycles Full, See-through and Parts only), '⋯', 'Backup & fixes' and 'Add a missing part'. The system filter <select> is hidden on phones, so 'Filter: show one system at a time' can't be done there at all. -> Rewrite the help rows to match the real labels: 'View button: tap to cycle Full car → See-through → Parts only', 'Systems: tap a system, then Show on car to see just that system', '⋯ More: How to use, Backup & fixes, Add a missing part'. Remove the Filter, Body and X-ray rows.

ui high [panel]: On flagged parts the owner can't tell which number to order. The panel shows Motorcraft PW-425 first with no warning. The suggested numbers come after it, and each carries the jargon 'suggested by verification, confirm on the car' packed into grey 11px text (ui-panel-flagged-phone/desk). Nothing marks which number is the wrong-fit one. -> When conf==='X', sort rows so isSug(x) rows come first and add use this one to each. Show the original non-suggested rows dimmed (opacity:.55) under a heading 'Old number, fits a different car'. Change the text to 'likely right — check it matches the old part'.
agent_notes: Model QC (+z = LH): The sides are consistent: +z is driver/LH for every named part, and the big layout calls are right. Intake is toward the firewall, exhaust toward the radiator, the timing and accessory drive are on the passenger (-z) end, the transaxle is on the driver end, the tank is under the rear seat and the muffler is at the back. The real problems are collisions and scale near the driver-side front: the battery is inside the headlamp and radiator, the master cylinder is behind the firewall inside the dash, the ABS unit is inside the LH tire and the PCM is far from the battery. The engine stack also has the valve cover and coil pack buried in the block, and the wheels are 0.26 lower than their hubs. The motor-mount explode vector is the only ex that points the wrong way.

model warn dash: The dash runs from x 2.97 to 4.57, so it pokes past the firewall into the intake manifold (x from 4.05), the throttle body and the cowl-mounted cabin filter (x 4.5). -> suggest {"pos": [3.3, 3.6, 0]}

model warn airbox: The box spans x 5.4–7.0, y 2.4–3.6, z 1.55–3.05 and overlaps the battery. At 1.6×1.2×1.5 (about 390×290×365 mm) it is also oversized. -> suggest {"pos": [5.9, 3.45, 1.55]}

model warn eng-block: The block plus head is 2.9 tall (0.70 m). With the oil pan and valve cover stacked on it the engine is 0.96 m tall, so the pan and valve cover have to sit inside the block to fit under the hood. -> suggest {"size": [1.9, 2.4, 2.5]}

ui med [nav]: On the phone, the app's only instructions ('How to use') are hidden behind a bare '⋯' button, and the mobile CSS hides the subtitle that holds the gesture hints (#top .sub{display:none}). After the coach dialog is dismissed, a first-time user has no visible way back to help. -> Change the ⋯ button's label to 'More' and put a visible '?' button (the #helpbtn style already exists, 36px wide) at the end of the first #tools .row that opens help. Or move bHelp out of #moreRow into the main row as '? Help'.

ui med [labels]: The button text 'View: Full' means nothing to a layperson, and you only find out what the other modes are by tapping it. The title tooltip ('Full car / See-through / Parts only') never appears on touch screens. -> Rename the states to 'Full car', 'See inside', 'Parts only' and set the button text to e.g. '👁 Full car'. On the first tap, show a toast such as 'See inside: body is see-through. Tap again for Parts only'.

ui med [panel]: When you open a part from List, Search or a system chip at 0% explode with the Full view, the part stays hidden inside the body. The car moves up behind the toolbar and you can't see which part was picked (ui-panel-phone: alternator not visible). select() only reveals the part when opts.reveal is set. -> Call select(m,{reveal:true}) from every list, search and chip handler. In select(), when reveal is set, also give the selected part a short pulse (animate the emissive between 0x8a4a10 and 0xffa040 three times).

ui med [visual]: On the phone, while a sheet is open, the camera view offset (innerHeight*0.28) pushes the car up under the search bar and buttons. The toolbar covers the roof and upper part of the car (every phone sheet screenshot). -> When a sheet is open on screens ≤700px, collapse #tools to the search field only (body.sheet-open #tools .row{display:none}). Lower the view offset to innerHeight*0.2 so the car sits in the visible band between the toolbar and the sheet.

ui med [labels]: Two different trust levels share the same grey 'number unconfirmed' badge: K (from Ford's catalog) and L (a best guess). The Help sheet's trust key shows two identical grey badges with different meanings (ui-help-desk). -> Set CONF.L to 'best guess, check first' and give it its own style, e.g. .cL{background:#4a2f1a;color:#ffd3a8}. Keep K as 'from Ford catalog'.

ui med [jargon]: The panel Notes and DIY tip are aimed at a parts clerk: 'NOT 8418 (SVT / late-04), NOT 8406 (05-07 Duratec). 6-groove pulley, 11 o clock plug, 2-ear mount' and 'Lester 8260 for this car, not 8418 or 8406'. The Vehicle facts use 'MTX-75', '4F27E', 'ZTW', 'VIN code 3', and Systems uses 'PCM' and 'degas bottle', all with no explanation. -> Put Notes inside <details><summary>Details for the parts counter</summary>. Take part numbers out of the tip text. Add a GLOSS map ({PCM:'engine computer',degas:'coolant overflow tank',Duratec:'the newer 2.0 engine, not yours',...}) and, on first use of each term, wrap it in <abbr title> with a dotted underline that shows the gloss when tapped.

ui med [touch]: Several touch targets are well under 44px. The inline part chips in the Systems text are about 24px tall (.chip padding 4px 10px, min-height:0). The '‹ All systems' back link has padding 0 and is about 18px tall. The system chip in the panel header is about 24px. -> Set .chip{padding:7px 12px;min-height:34px;line-height:1.3}. Set .back{padding:10px 12px 10px 0;min-height:44px;font-size:14px}. In the systems prose, add line-height:2.1 to the paragraph so the larger chips don't overlap.

ui med [visual]: On the phone at 60% explode, the exploded parts run off both sides of the screen (headlamps and wheels cut off in ui-exploded-phone). The camera doesn't pull back as the car spreads out. -> In the render loop, move the camera back along its direction as the explode amount grows on narrow screens: const k=1+t*(camera.aspect<0.7?0.55:0.15); camera.position.copy(target).addScaledVector(dir, baseDist*k).
